objective.summary: Design a layered Bitcoin instrument system that locks a meaningful share of BTC into long-term time-anchored bearer bonds and gradually introduces smaller, cash-like denominations, increasing illiquid supply and nudging volatility down over long horizons so Bitcoin becomes more usable as everyday money without assuming perfect stability.
goals: Create a deep-savings layer of Bitcoin-backed bearer bonds with long maturities (e.g., 10 years).
Roll out a denomination ladder from large to small BTC notes in phased stages.
Increase the share of BTC that is illiquid and committed to long-term holding.
Reduce realized BTC volatility over long horizons, while accepting that short-term swings remain.
Provide older and traditional users with familiar, certificate-like instruments for holding BTC exposure.

economic: Bearer bonds must be fully backed 1:1 by provable BTC reserves or protocol-level time-locked UTXOs.
Principal is denominated in BTC, not fiat; fiat value remains floating.
No hard peg mechanism is introduced; volatility is nudged, not eliminated.
regulatory: Assume instruments are treated as securities or investment products in most jurisdictions.
Issuers must comply with AML/KYC and reporting requirements appropriate for securities and crypto-asset services.
Custody, solvency, and redemption terms must be auditable and clearly disclosed.
technical: Prefer native Bitcoin features (e.g., time-locked contracts) for on-chain enforcement where feasible.
Aggregate transparency is required: publish periodic data on BTC reserves and outstanding bonds.
System must support interoperation with existing payment rails and custodial wallets.

deep_savings_layer.name: Long-Term Bitcoin Bearer Bonds
deep_savings_layer.description: A deep-savings layer where significant BTC amounts are locked for long horizons via bearer-style bonds or certificates, reducing tradable supply and reinforcing savings behavior.

features.principal_definition: Fixed BTC amount payable to the bearer at or after maturity, or on demand according to defined rules.
yield_options: pure BTC exposure (no explicit coupon, only BTC price movement)
optional premium or yield at maturity (in BTC or fiat), if the issuer chooses

possible_mechanisms: script-level time-lock (CLTV/CSV) with fixed unlock height/time
contractual 'do not touch' policy with regulatory oversight and audits

denomination_ladder.name: BTC Denomination Ladder
denomination_ladder.description: A family of fixed-denomination BTC bearer bonds/notes, rolled out from large to small units over multiple phases to match risk, complexity, and adoption readiness.

form_factors: physical certificate / banknote with advanced security features
digitally represented bearer claims where legally acceptable
verification: public BTC address and/or note ID encoded as QR or NFC for balance checking
strong anti-counterfeiting (secure substrate, holograms, tamper-evident key covers, etc.)
behavior: bearer-style: possession of the note implies right to redemption
compatible with long-term storage in safes, safety deposit boxes, and estate planning

everyday_payments_layer.name: Everyday-Use & Payments Layer
everyday_payments_layer.description: A layer where users make day-to-day transactions while being shielded from most BTC volatility, via payment processors, stable-value instruments, or smaller notes.
patterns: Use small-denomination BTC bearer notes directly where accepted for in-person payments.
Use payment processors or wallets that price goods in local fiat (CAD, USD, etc.), settling to or from BTC in the background.
Optionally integrate fiat-pegged stablecoins or tokenized bank money that may be partially backed by BTC reserves.
volatility_handling: Hedge BTC price risk at the processor/issuer level using derivatives or reserve management.
Offer users clear fiat equivalents at transaction time, even if underlying settlement uses BTC.

rollout_phases.label: Phase 1 – Large Saver Bonds
primary_objectives: Establish legal, custody, and tax frameworks for BTC-backed bearer bonds.
Demonstrate secure issuance, storage, and redemption.
Lock an initial stake of BTC into long-term savings, increasing illiquid supply.
success_indicators: non-trivial share of BTC supply held in Phase 1 bonds
no major custody failures or redemption disputes
clear regulatory treatment in key jurisdictions

rollout_phases.label: Phase 2 – Mid-Denomination Notes
target_users: older users comfortable with certificates and bank-style products
primary_objectives: Expand deep-savings participation beyond early adopters and institutions.
Increase overall illiquid BTC supply and strengthen the deep-savings backbone.
Start limited circulation of notes in high-trust environments (banks, credit unions, family offices).
success_indicators: growth in the share of BTC locked in Phases 1 + 2 instruments
positive user feedback from older/traditional savers
no systemic redemption or liquidity issues as volumes grow

rollout_phases.label: Phase 3 – Small Retail Notes
instruments: 0.01 BTC notes (savings or free-floating bearer instruments)
0.001 BTC notes for small savings and limited everyday spending
primary_objectives: Make BTC exposure tangible and psychologically accessible to the broad public.
Allow notes to function both as spendable tokens (where accepted) and as small savings certificates.
Reach an S-curve saturation level where a significant fraction of BTC supply is held in bearer instruments.
success_indicators: steady uptake of small notes across demographics
measurable increase in illiquid supply share attributable to retail bearer notes
no widespread confusion about denominations, maturity, or redemption

illiquid_supply_dynamics.mechanism: Every issued bearer bond or note that is designed as a multi-year savings instrument effectively pushes BTC from the liquid trading pool into the illiquid pool.
illiquid_supply_dynamics.expected_trend: Over 10–15 years, the share of BTC held in long-term bonds and similar deep-savings structures grows, raising total illiquid supply.
illiquid_supply_dynamics.empirical_reference: Empirical data already show illiquid BTC supply rising into the 70–75% range; this design aims to formalize and extend that trend via structured products.

volatility_dynamics.mechanism: With a larger fraction of supply locked in long-term commitments and more users interacting through notes and payment layers, fewer coins are subject to short-term speculative trading.
volatility_dynamics.expected_trend: Realized volatility remains high relative to fiat currencies but can trend downward over multi-year periods as market structure and deep savings mature.
limitations: Short-term macro shocks and sentiment will still cause sharp moves in the freely tradable float.
The system introduces no hard peg or automatic stabilizer, so there is no guarantee of narrow price bands.

everyday_currency_implications.goal: Make BTC sufficiently less volatile, and sufficiently well-wrapped in user-friendly instruments, that it becomes practical to use as a store of value and, in layered form, as a medium of exchange.
approach: Deep-savings bonds for long-term store of value.
Smaller bearer notes for tangible, cash-like exposure.
Payment and stable-value layers to insulate everyday transactions from residual volatility.

user_targets: older adults uncomfortable with pure digital wallets
traditional savers familiar with bonds, CDs, and paper certificates
users who prefer tangible instruments over app-only experiences

form_factors: paper-like notes that feel similar to banknotes or bond certificates
clear face values in BTC with simple explanatory text
mental_models: describe instruments as 'Bitcoin savings certificates' or 'Bitcoin bearer bonds' rather than as speculative trading instruments
encourage 'buy-and-hold' deep savings instead of constant monitoring and trading
risk_perception: reduce anxiety about self-custody through institutional custody and clear redemption channels
give users a physical object to hold, store, and bequeath, aligning with long-term savings behavior

instrument_classification: treat BTC-backed bearer bonds/notes as securities or investment products as per local law
align with frameworks used for crypto funds, ETPs, and asset-backed notes
issuer_obligations: maintain audited BTC reserves matching outstanding instruments
implement robust AML/KYC for issuance and redemption, especially on higher denominations
file required disclosures and prospectuses for public offerings
provide clear risk disclosures on BTC volatility, custody, and redemption terms
transparency: publish regular reserve attestations or audits
publish aggregate statistics on outstanding instruments and associated BTC reserves
communicate changes to terms, fees, or redemption policies well in advance

open_questions: What minimum and maximum share of BTC supply in bearer bonds would meaningfully impact volatility without unduly concentrating liquidity risk?
How should the system handle lost or destroyed physical notes, both economically and legally?
What mix of on-chain time-locks versus contractual commitments is optimal given regulatory and technical constraints?
How should interest or yield (if any) be structured so as not to create unsustainable obligations or disguised leverage?
